analysis.title: Lear Corp. (LEA): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: GS calls Lear's 3Q26 report relatively solid: 3Q EBIT and implied 4Q EBIT guidance are both about in line with the Street (FactSet). EPS was well above the Street, and revenue was somewhat lower.
Lear lowered its 2026 revenue guidance to $23.4-23.8 bn from $23.5-24.0 bn but kept the core operating income outlook of $1,080-1,200 mn.
Implied 4Q26 guidance at the midpoint is below the Street on revenue ($5,745 mn vs $5,949 mn) and above it on margin (4.8% vs 4.6%). Implied EBIT is $274 mn vs the Street at $273 mn.
Lear had growth over market in both segments in 3Q: 4% in Seating and 2% in E-Systems (5% excluding wind-down business). Globally it was 4%.
By region, Lear grew 4% over market in North America and 12% in Europe, and underperformed the market by 18% in China (8% under including non-consolidated sales).
Content per vehicle rose about 3% y/y to $682 in North America and about 11% to $505 in Europe and Africa.
Full-year guidance assumes global auto production down 2% and down 1% on a Lear-weighted basis. This reflects weaker China and North America and an uptick in Europe.
CY26 FCF guidance was lowered to $565-665 mn from $590-690 mn. Lear still expects more than $350 mn of share repurchases in 2026.
The press release cites replacement and new awards for Seating and E-Systems, including with Chinese domestic OEMs.
Lear announced a CFO succession plan. Jason Cardew retires effective December 31, 2027, and Jared Fedele becomes CFO as of March 1, 2027.
GS key call questions: production environment and industry backdrop, growth over market and regional trends, and input costs and the margin outlook.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Neutral rating and $124 12-month target, based on 7x normalized EPS of $17.75. The price was $117.38, which implies 5.6% upside.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 revenue reported $5,773 mn (+2% y/y, +2% organic, -7% q/q) vs GS estimate $5,818 mn and Street (FactSet) estimate $5,809 mn.
3Q26 adjusted core operating income reported $256 mn (4.4% margin) vs GS estimate $254 mn (4.4%) and Street estimate $255 mn (4.4%).
3Q26 adjusted operating EPS reported $3.71 vs Street estimate $3.32 and GS estimate $3.21.
3Q26 free cash flow reported $158 mn. Lear spent $175 mn on share repurchases and $38 mn on dividends in the quarter.

3Q26 segment revenue reported: Seating $4,326.1 mn (1.9% below Street), E-Systems $1,446.9 mn (2.7% above Street). Non-GAAP segment operating income reported: Seating $273.7 mn vs $277.8 mn Street, E-Systems $69.1 mn vs $60.6 mn Street.

CY26 guidance (company): revenue $23.35-23.75 bn (midpoint $23.55 bn vs GS estimate $23.795 bn and Street estimate $23.793 bn), core operating income $1,080-1,200 mn (midpoint $1,140 mn, 4.8% margin vs GS estimate $1,145 mn and Street estimate $1,139 mn), FCF $565-665 mn (midpoint $615 mn vs GS estimate $628.3 mn and Street estimate $633 mn).

Implied 4Q26 guidance at the midpoint: revenue $5,745 mn (-4.1% y/y), adjusted EBIT $274 mn, margin 4.8%. Street estimates are $5,949 mn / $273 mn / 4.6%, and GS estimates are $5,945 mn / $281 mn / 4.7%.
GS estimates EPS of $15.05 for 12/26E, $16.70 for 12/27E and $18.40 for 12/28E. Quarterly estimates are $3.21 for 9/26E (3Q26 actual since reported at $3.71), $3.68 for 12/26E and $3.73 for 3/27E.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Lear's full-year guidance assumes weaker China and North America production and a modest uptick in Europe. The prior assumption was down 2% globally and down less than 2% Lear-weighted.

risk_factors: The auto cycle could be more or less positive than GS expects.
Lear could outgrow or undergrow underlying auto production by more than GS expects.
Lear could gain or lose market share in Seating and/or E-Systems.
Tariff impacts could be larger or smaller than expected.
Margins carry upside and downside risk. Wages, supply chain issues and competition could hurt margin targets, while cost actions such as increased automation could help.
Underperformance against the market in China (down 18%).
